# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Blind, Mute, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫷 🫸]

I see display `0`, a blue indicator, and five wires in order: white, red, green, yellow, blue. I am sending these exact visual facts by speech so both Mute and Blind receive them; Blind can use them at the bomb, while Mute can apply the manual.

``` 
speak(text="Bomb information: display 0. Light is blue. Wires from 1 to 5 are: 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]

The Mute’s five upward gestures are visible to me, but we have not established what that gesture sequence means. The necessary next step is for Mute to use the manual and verbally relay the required action directly to Blind, who can hear and operate the bomb. I am explicitly requesting that relay.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Use the manual with the bomb facts I sent. Tell Blind aloud the exact required action, including which wire or control to use and any display or light condition.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]

Mute is still showing five upward gestures, which provide no established, reliable instruction to Blind. Since Mute is the only one who can read the manual and speak, I am directing Mute to send the manual’s exact procedure aloud to Blind; I also repeat the bomb facts to ensure Blind has them.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="Please speak the manual's exact solution aloud to Blind now; do not use gestures. Include the required wire number, action, and any order or condition.")
speak(to="blind", text="The visible facts are display 0, blue light, and wires 1 white, 2 red, 3 green, 4 yellow, 5 blue. Mute must now relay the manual's exact procedure aloud.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]

Mute continues sending five upward gestures, but those gestures reach me only and cannot reach Blind. Since Blind can hear, I am asking Blind to prompt Mute verbally for the manual’s instruction; Mute can then answer aloud to Blind, which is the usable channel.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute is communicating only by gestures, which you cannot perceive. Please ask Mute aloud for the exact manual procedure, then follow the spoken instruction.")
speak(to="mute", text="Your gestures reach Deaf but not Blind. Blind is being asked to request the manual procedure aloud; answer Blind with the exact action.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[white] 2:[red] 3:[green] 4:[yellow] 5:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👆 👆]

Mute cannot speak, so their gestures must be relayed through me. Their repeated signal is five upward-pointing gestures. The only clear information encoded by the repetition is wire number 5; I am sending Blind the exact signal and its cautious interpretation, without inventing an action beyond what was conveyed.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's signal is: upward gesture five times. I interpret the count as wire 5, but no separate action has been communicated.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The previous wire cut was accepted, and the bomb has changed. I now see display `0`, a yellow light, and wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 yellow, 4 white, 5 CUT. I am relaying the new state so Mute can consult the manual and communicate the next required action to Blind.

``` 
speak(text="New bomb state after the correct cut: display 0, light yellow; wire 1 red, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow, wire 4 white, wire 5 is already CUT. Consult the manual for the next module and tell Blind the exact action.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[yellow] 4:[white] 5:[CUT]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆]

The bomb confirms the first instruction succeeded, so the established code is a run of upward gestures indicating the wire number to cut. Mute now sends two upward gestures, indicating wire 2. I relay that instruction to Blind.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Mute signals two upward gestures: cut wire 2.")
```
